sections.label: Re-employment age raised to 67
sections.summary: The re-employment age will be raised from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: First, the re-employment age will be raised from 65 to 67.

sections.label: Re-employment age change details
sections.summary: From 1 July 2017 the re-employment age rises from 65 to 67 for those born on or after 1 July 1952, supported by the Additional SEC scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The first key change is that the re-employment age will be raised from 65 to 67 with effect from 1 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The new re-employment age of 67 will apply to those who turn 65 on or after 1 July 2017; in other words, those born on or after 1 July 1952.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: To encourage employers to re-employ employees beyond the re-employment age, which is 65 today, the Government currently provides a 3% additional wage offset.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This scheme, the Additional Special Employment Credit (SEC) scheme, benefits about 120,000 Singaporean employees aged 65 and above every year.

sections.label: Removing wage reduction option
sections.summary: Tripartite partners agreed to remove the option for employers to reduce wages at age 60 from 1 July 2017, and the Bill repeals section 5.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: In 2011, 98.5% of companies with employees aged 60 and over did not reduce the wages of employees at age 60.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Hence, the tripartite partners have agreed to remove this option for employers with effect from 1 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This Bill is the result of tripartite efforts over the last few years to strike this delicate balance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We recognise that there are older employees in all sectors and occupations, with different circumstances and needs, therefore, not all of which can be addressed by this Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, continue to work closely with our tripartite partners to continue to enhance employment opportunities for older workers and to build age-friendly workplaces in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First is the repeal of section 5 of the current Act which effectively means abolishing the provision which had allowed employers to reduce up to 10% of salary once an employee reaches the age of 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, an employer who finds suitable employment for an employee, who is supposed to be re-employed, with another employer is considered to have fulfilled his obligation under the Bill.

sections.label: Funding for older worker schemes
sections.summary: The Government has funded initiatives such as WorkPro, SEC and additional credits to support hiring of mature and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government has funded and rolled out a series of initiatives and funding, such as WorkPro, SEC and additional credits to support the hiring of mature and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to continue these schemes and funding, especially those that are due to expire and even enhance them, bearing in mind we are confronted with a silver tsunami.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I have previously raised in this House for the increase of EAP and I am glad that we will be seeing a positive adjustment in this respect.

sections.label: Written notice before termination
sections.summary: Clause 4 requires employers to give written notice before termination where they do not intend to re-employ due to unsatisfactory performance or medical unfitness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 4 states that "where an employer does not intend to re-employ an employee past the retirement age because the employee does not either have satisfactory work performance or is not medically fit, the employer must give the employee written notice as far as is reasonably practicable before termination." Section 8 of the current Act provides some remedies, which is, for the employee to write in to MOM and let MOM decide if they have been unfairly dismissed or denied re-employment.

sections.label: Discouraged older workers framework
sections.summary: In 2015 there were 8,700 discouraged workers, 69% aged 50 and over, prompting a relook at frameworks tackling discriminatory employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, there were 8,700 discouraged workers in Singapore who would like to work but had given up looking for a job because they feel that their chances are almost nil, according to the 2015 Labour Force Survey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Sixty-nine percent of those discouraged were aged 50 and over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To meet this gap, we should relook at the framework for tackling discriminatory employment practices in general, not only for ageist prejudice but for other forms of prejudice on grounds of gender, race, religion, disability status or ex-offender status, for example.

sections.label: TAFEP complaints and older workers
sections.summary: The passage states TAFEP can escalate complaints to MOM, that some sticks may be ineffective, and that employees may not complain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Right now, we have a system where employees can complain to TAFEP and TAFEP can then escalate complaints to MOM which can wield the stick of employment and work pass access as well as moral suasion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, for companies that are not open to moral exhortations or which do not require Employment Passes or Work Permits, these sticks may be ineffective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, going further upstream, there could be many employees who know or suspect that they have been on the receiving end of discriminatory practices but who would not want to complain to TAFEP for many reasons, not only a lack of confidence or timidity but also perhaps a lack of confidence that they could prove their case in a "my word against yours" sort of situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As a country, we have a long way to go to shift our labour market norms towards embracing the idea of people working till well into their 60s and perhaps older, if they choose to do so.

sections.label: Residents outside labour force aged 60
sections.summary: The passage states the share of residents outside the labour force aged 60 or older rose from 35% in 2006 to 44% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2006, 35% of residents outside the labour force were 60 or older; over the decade, this proportion has grown steadily, with the latest reported figure for 2016 showing 44% of residents outside the labour force belonging to this age group.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With figures of this magnitude, expanding opportunities for re-employment beyond the current threshold of 65 years is clearly welcomed and necessary.

sections.label: Term contracts for older employees
sections.summary: The passage states 25% of resident employees aged 60 and over were on term contracts in June 2007 and 21% in June 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In June 2007, 25% of resident employees aged 60 and over were on term contracts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Almost a decade later, in June 2015, we still have 21% of resident employees aged 60 and above on term contracts.

sections.label: Re-employment offset and late payments
sections.summary: The passage states employers re-employing Singaporean workers aged 65 and above receive an offset, and Business Times reported more late payments last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since 2015, employers who voluntarily re-employ Singaporean workers aged 65 and above have been receiving an additional offset of up to 3% of an employee's monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the economy is weak at the moment and employers are facing several challenges.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the Business Times reported yesterday that in the worst performance in five years, last year saw more companies slow to make payment and fewer paying on time.

sections.label: Legislation and differing business conditions
sections.summary: The passage states existing legislation and proposed changes do not consider that businesses may differ and operate under different conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the moment, neither the existing legislation nor the proposed changes take into consideration the fact that businesses may be very different and may also be operating under very different conditions.

sections.label: EAP requirement and employer burden
sections.summary: The passage states the tripartite guidelines call for a maximum EAP amount, but the EAP requirement seems to ignore economic circumstances and employer conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although paragraph 25(c) of the tripartite guidelines has stated that, and I quote, "There should be a maximum EAP amount to moderate the financial burden on employers", at the moment, the EAP requirement seems to ignore both the prevailing economic circumstances and the specific conditions under which a particular employer might be struggling.

sections.label: Life expectancy in Singapore
sections.summary: Average life expectancy rose for females from about 63 years in 1957 to 85 in 2015, and for males from about 59 to 80.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our average life expectancy for females increased from about 63 years in 1957 to 85 years in 2015, and for males, it rose from about 59 years to 80 years over the same period.

sections.label: Work beyond age 62
sections.summary: The Bill lets capable and willing Singaporeans work beyond 62 up to 67, and allows re-employment contracts for workers aged 62.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given today's economic climate and the increasing pressure to increase productivity to remain competitive, we must examine ways through which we can maximise our labour resources and ensure that our workforce remains dynamic in an era of rapid movement and change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Bill ensures that Singaporeans who are capable and willing to work beyond the age of 62 now have the option to do so till they are 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the same time, the amendment to this Bill can allow other employers to have access to the pool of experienced, evergreen workers since re-employment contracts can be offered to workers who have reached the age of 62 if their existing employers are unable to find a suitable position or vacancy for re-employment in their company.

sections.label: Longer re-employment contract term
sections.summary: The law should extend re-employment contract renewal beyond one year to a three-year contract period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Fourthly, the law should look into extending the re-employment contract term to beyond a one-year renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There should be a longer contract period of three years, in view of the increasing life expectancy of Singapore's workforce and also in the interests of giving our older workforce a greater sense of security.

sections.label: Training support programmes
sections.summary: The Bill can achieve lifelong employability only if workers tap Government training support programmes such as SkillsFuture and Workforce Skills Qualification training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Only if workers tap on the various training support programmes by the Government, such as SkillsFuture, the Workforce Skills Qualification training and others, can this Bill then achieve its intent of lifelong employability.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age history
sections.summary: The Bill gives no job guarantee; workers must reskill, employers must change mindsets, and the Government set 67 as the target age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On the part of workers, this Bill does not give any job guarantee unless the workers constantly upgrade and reskill to ensure relevancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Employers need to change their mindset to get rid of any prejudices they may have of older workers and change the work culture and processes to be more inclusive of older workers, instead of clamouring for more foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Government must continue to support training to ensure our local workforce have the opportunities to upgrade and reskill for lifelong employability and calibrate its manpower policies to encourage a strong Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Back in 1993, when Parliament amended the law to raise the retirement age from 55 to 60, the Government set 67 as the target retirement age to be achieved in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The retirement age was raised to 62 in 1999.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And then in 2012, when Parliament amended the law to set the re-employment age at 65, the Government again set the target age, now for re-employment age, to 67.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It has taken five years to move the extension and 23 years in total to reach the 67 target.

sections.label: Life expectancy in 1993
sections.summary: In 1993, the average life expectancy of Singaporeans was around 77 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 1993, the average life expectancy of Singaporeans was around 77 years.

sections.label: Re-employment age extension anxiety
sections.summary: Extending the re-employment age to 67 means senior Singaporeans wanting to keep working face contract review or renewal anxiety four times from 63 to 66.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the extension of the re-employment age to 67, this means senior Singaporeans who would like to continue working would suffer twice the anxiety of contract review or renewal, four times from 63 to 66 years of age.

sections.label: CPF LIFE payout age statement
sections.summary: Manpower Minister Lim Swee Say said in September 2015 that the CPF LIFE payout age of 65 would not be raised when re-employment age rises to 67.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The sixth point: Manpower Minister Lim Swee Say said during the General Election in September 2015 that the payout age of 65 for the CPF LIFE scheme would not be raised when the re-employment age is raised to 67.

sections.label: Explaining 23 years to raise retirement age
sections.summary: The Government should explain to Singaporeans why it took 23 years to raise the effective retirement age to the targeted 67.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In summary, the Government should explain to Singaporeans why it took all of 23 years to raise the effective retirement age to the targeted 67.

sections.label: Questions on senior worker policies
sections.summary: The passage asks why retirement age stays at 62, why medical benefits are unprotected, whether burden of proof should shift, and why not earlier CPF payouts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, why leave the retirement age stuck at 62 now when employers have grown accustomed to senior Singaporeans working to 65?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Four, why are the medical benefits for senior workers not protected for re-employment?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Five, should the Ministry depart from the convention of placing the burden of proof on the worker for senior workers seeking recourse on being rejected for re-employment due to alleged poor work performance?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Six, since CPF LIFE payouts are now delinked from the effective retirement age, why not let senior workers get their payout earlier and trust them to invest in themselves?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Retirement age policy is a critical tool that could be used to effectively tackle many of the economic, social and psychological issues related to the ageing population.

sections.label: Abolishing salary adjustments
sections.summary: Abolishing salary adjustments is important because wages should reflect a worker's job scope and output.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, the abolishing of the salary adjustments is important because wages should reflect a worker's job scope and output.

sections.label: Reviewing SEC wage offset
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider continuing the 3% additional wage offset under SEC and reviewing the SEC ceiling cap for older workers earning over $4,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Government consider continuing the additional wage offset of 3% of wages support given under SEC?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Government also review the ceiling cap for the SEC, so that the wage offset can be given to companies that employ older workers earning more than $4,000 a month?

sections.label: Support for re-employment age amendments
sections.summary: The speaker supports amendments to the Retirement and Re-employment Bill raising the re-employment age from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I support the amendments to the Retirement and Re-employment Bill, raising the re-employment age from 65 to 67.

sections.label: Longer lives and repealed wage cut
sections.summary: Raising the re-employment age from 65 to 67 is timely, and a provision allowing wage cuts at age 60 will be repealed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With Singaporeans living longer and in better health, raising the re-employment age from 65 to 67 is timely and will allow them to continue their work longer, contributing their valuable expertise and experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am very glad to note that an outdated provision, which allows employers to cut employees' wages at age 60, will be repealed.

sections.label: SEC scheme for older workers
sections.summary: The SEC scheme gives employers up to 8% of an older employee's monthly wage for those aged 55 and above earning up to $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There is already an incentive scheme for employers to hire older workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is the SEC scheme which provides employers up to 8% of an older employee's monthly wage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The scheme targets companies which hire employees aged 55 and above and who earn up to $4,000 a month.

sections.label: Act effective from July 2017
sections.summary: From 1 July 2017, the Retirement and Re-employment Act takes effect, extending the re-employment age from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, from 1 July 2017, the Retirement and Re-employment Act will take effect, with the re-employment age being extended from 65 to 67.

sections.label: Employer offer if no position
sections.summary: If no position can be found, the employer must offer a substantial amount of EAP or help the employee get another job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If no position can be found, the employer has to offer a substantial amount of EAP or help the employee get a job at another company.

sections.label: Legislations permanent, schemes temporary
sections.summary: The Government had introduced wage credit schemes to lighten companies' burdens, but legislations are permanent while schemes are temporary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the past, the Government had introduced wage credit schemes to lighten companies' burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, we all know that legislations are there forever, they are permanent; but schemes are temporary.

sections.label: Re-employment age extension limits
sections.summary: Extending the re-employment age by two years does not mean all older workers can work another two years, as some suitable positions may become obsolete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Extending the re-employment age by two years does not mean that all older workers would be able to work for another two years, especially in this critical period of economic restructuring where some positions which were suitable for older workers may become obsolete.

sections.label: Bus captain retirement ages
sections.summary: In 2013 SBS Transit raised bus captains' retirement age to 67, and last year SMRT raised their re-employment age to 69.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2013, the Singapore Bus Services (SBS) Transit raised the retirement age of their bus captains to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT) raised the re-employment age of bus captains to 69.

sections.label: No wage cut at 60
sections.summary: The speaker hopes more companies recognise these benefits and applauds that mature workers turning 60 will no longer face a wage cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that more companies can recognise these benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would also like to applaud the change that there will no longer be a wage cut for mature workers turning 60.

sections.label: WorkPro Job Redesign Grant
sections.summary: Under the enhanced WorkPro scheme effective last July, the Job Redesign Grant helps companies create easier, safer and smarter jobs for mature workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As part of the enhanced WorkPro scheme which came into effect last July, there is the Job Redesign (JR) Grant to help companies create easier, safer and smarter jobs for our mature workers.

sections.label: Age discrimination amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments to the Bill reinforce that no worker should be discriminated against because of their age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the Bill serve to reinforce that no worker should be discriminated because of their age.

sections.label: Raising re-employment age benefits
sections.summary: Raising the re-employment age from the cap of 65 to 67 brings benefits to both the economy and the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Raising the re-employment age from the cap of 65 to 67 brings benefits both to our economy and to our workforce.

sections.label: Seniors working past 65
sections.summary: MP asks if studies show how many seniors work past 65 by choice or necessity, and whether CPF payout eligibility age will rise to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The rising costs of living may also mean that many have no choice but to work well beyond the age of 65, sometimes into their 70s, as you have heard, and even 80s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With this in mind, has the Ministry conducted any studies to reveal statistics on how many of our seniors work beyond the age of 65 because they want to, or because they have to and the reasons they have to work beyond 65?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, the main question I have been asked about this Bill is whether we will also be increasing the CPF Retirement Account payout eligibility age, which is currently at age 65 and we might be increasing it to 67.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I must applaud the tripartite partners for their effort in bringing about the change, that is, the extension of re-employment age to 67 and also to ensure responsible re-employment on the part of the employers instead of taking the easy way out by paying EAP.

sections.label: Help for older workers
sections.summary: The law changes are timely, but measures are needed to help older workers who lost employment before the law takes effect.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Though the changes to the law are, indeed, timely and a most welcome step for a more inclusive and progressive workforce, measures have to be taken to help those older workers who have fallen out of employment now and until the law takes effect.

sections.label: Reviewing wage support schemes
sections.summary: MOM could review whether wage support schemes effectively encourage companies to hire workers beyond 65, or introduce age-tiered support.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even though there are various wage support schemes for companies to keep older workers in a job, be it those 55 and above and those 65 and above, perhaps MOM could review if these measures have been effective, especially to encourage companies to hire workers beyond 65, or should there be an enhanced wage support scheme that is tiered based on age band?

sections.label: Ageing gracefully and retirement age
sections.summary: Singapore can be a lifestyle hub for ageing gracefully, and MOM should consider raising retirement age to 65 and re-employment without age limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore can be a lifestyle hub for one to age gracefully and it can bring about collective economic value and essentially doing well for our ageing population by creating jobs of such kind.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also hope that MOM will consider upping the retirement age to 65 at a suitable time in the medium term and allow for re-employment without age limit.

sections.label: Foreign worker quota for seniors
sections.summary: With growing grey waves, MOM is asked to consider a foreign worker quota tied to older Singaporeans employed, without affecting younger workforce opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the growing grey waves, will MOM consider having a quota on the foreign workers to older Singaporeans employed without affecting the opportunities for our younger workforce?

sections.label: Anti-discrimination laws on age
sections.summary: MOM could consider anti-discrimination laws, especially on age, to safeguard older jobseekers if persuasive efforts are slow.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notably, MOM could consider anti-discrimination laws, especially on age, as it is more prevalent as a constant bugbear so as to safeguard the interest of our growing older population seeking jobs, should the persuasive effort yield be low and slow.

sections.label: Section 7B re-employment entitlements
sections.summary: A Member asks whether section 7B can be deleted or amended so re-employed workers do not face cuts in entitlements tied to length of service.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three, in regard to section 7B, can I clarify if we can delete or amend the subsection so that re-employed workers will not see a cut in their entitlements that are tied to length of service?

sections.label: Section 7C employer obligations
sections.summary: A Member asks whether, under section 7C, the current employer must seek employment opportunities from another employer for re-employed staff.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Four, with reference to section 7C, does the current employer have an obligation to seek employment opportunities from another employer for the re-employed staff?

sections.label: Age-friendly hiring and salary revisions
sections.summary: The passage stresses providing employment opportunities to older workers and notes employers can no longer make indiscriminate downward salary revisions near retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is of utmost importance is that to continue to provide employment opportunities to these older workers, be it men or women, and for companies to embrace age-neutral, age-friendly hiring practices and create a fertile environment for older workers to age gracefully with pride and dignity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am particularly heartened that an employer can no longer make indiscriminate downward revisions of the salaries of employees once they are nearing retirement age.

sections.label: Section 7(3) reasonable period notice
sections.summary: A Member quotes section 7(3) on written notice before terminating employment and asks what a reasonable period is.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 4, section 7(3) states that, I quote, "Where an employer does not intend to re-employ an employee because the employee does not meet the criteria in subsection (1)(b), then as far as it is reasonably practicable, the employer must give the employee a written notice of that intention within a reasonable period before terminating the employee's employment." What is a "reasonable period"?

sections.label: EAP payment and reasonable attempts
sections.summary: A Member asks how much payment is sufficient and fair and what reasonable attempts and tripartite guidelines under section 7C mean.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, while I support clause 7 that makes amendments to section 7C to provide EAP, there is the question of how much payment is sufficient and fair and what constitutes reasonable attempts made by the employer in accordance with the tripartite guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry elaborate on what reasonable attempts may be and what these tripartite guidelines are?

sections.label: Key amendments in the Bill
sections.summary: The passage lists key amendments: raising the re-employment age ceiling from 65 to 67, repealing wage reduction at age 60, and allowing re-employment beyond the immediate company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, on the Bill itself, I am very happy, like all my fellow Parliamentary colleagues, about the key amendments: the one raising the re-employment age ceiling from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Second, repealing the power of employers to reduce wages at age 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, allowing employers to offer re-employment job positions that go beyond the immediate company or organisation, after due efforts have been made within the immediate company, to workers who are due for re-employment.

sections.label: Reducing cost of mature workers
sections.summary: Calls for extending employer wage subsidies like SEC and educating companies on tapping every worker regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Reduce net business cost of employing mature workers, for example ‒ and this has been mentioned by both the Minister and the other Members ‒ through an extension of employer wage subsidies, such as SEC or the additional SEC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Next, step up efforts to educate companies on the implications of the peaking of the Singaporean workforce in the coming five years, and to help them find ways to tap on every worker, regardless of age, to the best extent.

sections.label: Speeding up job matching
sections.summary: Says job-matching clearance speed must increase to avoid a build-up of structurally unemployed workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If increasing flux raises displacement risk, then we must find ways to increase the clearance speed of our job-matching mechanism so that we can avoid a build-up of a pool of structurally unemployed workers.

sections.label: Labour laws keeping up
sections.summary: States labour laws must keep up with changes so risks and rewards stay fairly balanced among businesses, workers and state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our labour laws and arrangements have to keep up with the changes and challenges, so as to ensure that the risks and rewards of enterprise and production continue to be fairly and sustainably balanced between businesses, working people and the state.

sections.label: Study raising effective working years
sections.summary: Proposes tripartite partners study how mature workers in different occupations may raise effective working years beyond national norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus far, we have largely gone on the basis of a single national statutory retirement age, followed by a standard duration of re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Chee How (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I believe that it is time also for the tripartite partners to study how mature workers in different occupation types may raise their effective working years beyond prevailing national statutory norms, for example, via industry-based or occupation-based norm setting.

sections.label: SEC scheme for older workers
sections.summary: Describes SEC giving companies incentive to hire workers above 55 earning up to $4,000, paying up to 8% of monthly wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, the SEC scheme provides some incentive for companies to hire older workers aged above 55 earning up to $4,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These companies will receive SEC of up to 8% of the employee's monthly wage.

sections.label: Re-employment age of 67
sections.summary: Notes rising labour force participation for ages 65 to 67 and the new re-employment age of 67 from 1 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For those 65 to 67 years, the labour force participation rate has risen from 30.9% in 2010 to 42.2% in 2015, although at a slower rate in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill specifies that from 1 July 2017, the new re-employment age of 67 will be applicable to those born on or after 1 July 1952.

sections.label: Future solutions for older workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether it is more critical to fast forward thinking on solutions for seniors and mid-40s workers, noting progress under Tricom, TAFEP and WorkPro Grants.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Now, would it not be more critical for us to fast forward our thinking on solutions for the future where generations of seniors, where workers in their mid-40s today, can continue to be meaningfully involved at the job market as they mature in the workforce?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: We should recognise that under the Tripartite Committee on Employability of Older Workers (Tricom) and TAFEP, some progress has been made through working with the tripartite partners and also with the WorkPro Grants.

sections.label: Reasons for not hiring seniors
sections.summary: The speaker believes three reasons primarily led to companies' reluctance to retain or hire older workers, the first being subconscious conjectures about seniors' roles and abilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Based on feedback, I believe there are three reasons that primarily led to the companies' reluctance in retaining or hiring older workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, our subconscious conjectures that associate our seniors to specific roles and worth of their abilities when they come of age.

sections.label: MOM and SPRING sharing practices
sections.summary: Mr Heng Chee How said it would be useful for MOM to work with SPRING Singapore to share practices and showcase companies, especially SMEs, that redesigned work scope for mature workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As pointed out by my colleague, Mr Heng Chee How, it will also be useful for MOM to work with SPRING Singapore to actively share practices and showcase how some companies, especially SMEs, have successfully implemented and redesigned their work scope to help mature workers manage new functions that they have not encountered previously.

sections.label: Three proposals for mature workers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes mandating internship opportunities for tertiary students, letting companies tap SkillsFuture credit for in-house training, and incentivising employers through skills development and work scope.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, to gradually mandate that tertiary students should have at least an opportunity for internships at companies in the public or private sectors through the course of their study.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, allow companies to tap on SkillsFuture credit and expertise to develop in-house training programmes relevant to their organisations or industries.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Third, incentivise the employers not through salary subsistence but skills development and work scope crafted for mature workers.

sections.label: Recognition of vendor course skills
sections.summary: The challenge after third party vendor courses is the level of recognition companies give to acquired skills, so industry-related training under SkillsFuture would incentivise continuous upgrading of workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The challenge that many individuals may face after gaining qualification from third party vendor courses in the open market is the level of recognition these companies are willing to accept on relevance and useful skills they have acquired.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, if company or industry-related training can be considered under SkillsFuture, it will provide the incentive, scope and flexibility for the companies to enable some focus on continuous upgrading of their workers.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says mature workers wishing to remain active face redundancy and no vacancy, and stands in support of the Bill, heartened by Minister Lim's remarks on extending the SEC.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It may not be time for many to hang up their boots as they are cruising in their career, but reality hits hard when the mature worker wishes to remain active at work, only to find that redundancy and no vacancy are the music that welcome them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It strikes a good balance between protecting our seniors and encouraging our employers to hire seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I stand in support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also very heartened to hear Minister Lim's remarks about considering extending the SEC.

sections.label: Hiring seniors beyond 67
sections.summary: The law does not stop companies from hiring seniors beyond 67, and the Pioneer Generation Office can visit seniors above 50 to share employment information and incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The law does not stop companies from hiring seniors beyond 67, even though they are not covered under the rules spelt out in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the Pioneer Generation Office can conduct household visits to seniors above 50 to share information on the current employment laws, as well as the incentives, such as the SEC, that can help them and that companies employ them.

sections.label: Tripartite talks on retirement age
sections.summary: When tripartite partners discussed raising the retirement age from 62 to 65 and beyond, all three parties objected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: When the tripartite partners sat down to talk about raising the retirement age from 62 to 65 and beyond, all three parties objected.

sections.label: Re-employment age adoption 2017
sections.summary: From 1 July 2017, Singapore will be ahead of Japan in the adoption of the re-employment age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Come 1 July 2017, we will be ahead of Japan in the adoption of the re-employment age.

sections.label: Re-employment age Singapore versus Japan
sections.summary: In July, Singapore's re-employment age will be 67, but in Japan it is still 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Come July, our re-employment age will be 67, but in Japan, it is still 65.

sections.label: Employment rate aged 65-69
sections.summary: With Singapore's re-employment age of 65, the employment rate of those aged 65-69 was 40.4% as of 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: What we discovered is that, with Singapore's re-employment age of 65, our employment rate of those aged 65-69 is 40.4%, as of 2015.

sections.label: Other countries' lower employment rates
sections.summary: All these countries, even without a retirement age, have employment rates for workers aged 65 to 69 significantly lower than Singapore's 40.4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: All of them, all these countries, even though they do not have a retirement age, their employment rates for workers aged 65 to 69 are all significantly lower than Singapore's 40.4%.

sections.label: CPF PEA and re-employment age
sections.summary: The CPF PEA and re-employment age remain related but are no longer identical, with the CPF PEA rising slower to 63 in 2012, 64 in 2015 and 65 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The two are still related, but they are no longer identical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: They are still related because both are related to the expected lifespan but yet at the same time, I think from 2012, you would notice that even though we raised the re-employment age to 65, the CPF PEA, in fact, went up much slower to 63 in 2012, 64 in 2015, and 65 only in 2018.

sections.label: CPF payout ages next year
sections.summary: Next year the ages will be 65 to 70 even though the re-employment age is 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Come next year, it will be ages 65 to 70 even though the re-employment age is 67.

sections.label: CPF LIFE interest rate
sections.summary: Putting their money under CPF LIFE lets them earn an interest rate of at least 4% per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: By putting their money under our CPF LIFE, they can earn an interest rate of at least 4% per year.

sections.label: Onus of proof on employer
sections.summary: On eligibility for re-employment, the onus of proof is on the employer to show proof.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On eligibility for re-employment, some Members have expressed concern on whether the onus of proof is on the workers or the employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I want to make it very clear that the onus is on the employer to show proof.

sections.label: MOM reinstatement or compensation
sections.summary: MOM will then come in to either reinstate re-employment or order compensation, based on the situation of the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: MOM will then come in to either reinstate re-employment or order compensation, based on the situation of the case.

sections.label: Re-employment entitlement for local workers
sections.summary: Re-employment is an entitlement covering all local workers, regardless of whether they are PMETs, high-wage or low-wage workers, who can approach the tripartite partners or MOM if they feel discriminated against under the Retirement and Re-employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Re-employment is an entitlement that covers all local workers, regardless of whether they are PMETs, high-wage or low-wage workers, they can all come to the tripartite partners or MOM if they feel that they had been discriminated against under the Retirement and Re-employment Act.

sections.label: ECT start date
sections.summary: ECT will come into effect on 1 April, before the re-employment age of 67 comes into effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: ECT will come into effect on 1 April, before the re-employment age of 67 comes into effect.

sections.label: Re-employment notification guidelines
sections.summary: Tripartite guidelines require at least three months' notice of eligibility and mutual consultation at least six months before re-employment or extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On the question about whether workers should be told much earlier if they are not eligible for re-employment, our tripartite guidelines stipulate that whether a person is eligible or not eligible for re-employment, he should be notified at least three months in advance, the longer the better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The guidelines dictate at least three months' notice for eligibility, and mutual consultation for at least six months prior to re-employment or extension of re-employment.

sections.label: Higher EAP quantum
sections.summary: Having extended the re-employment period from three to five years, the EAP quantum would be higher if the employer cannot offer re-employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Having extended the re-employment period from three to five years, the EAP quantum would be higher now, in the event the employer is not able to offer re-employment.

sections.label: Financial hardship EAP claims
sections.summary: Cases of companies in financial hardship unable to pay EAP can go to the Employment Claims Tribunal, which will rule after seeing the difficulty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan asked what if a company in financial hardship is not able to pay EAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Those cases can go to Employment Claims Tribunal and the Tribunal will then rule, after they have seen whether the company is, indeed, in such great difficulty that it is not able to pay the EAP.

sections.label: TAFEP investigations and age definitions
sections.summary: TAFEP watches companies more closely for pervasive HR discrimination practices, and retirement age involves same job, same pay while re-employment age does not necessarily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Once TAFEP does the investigation, if it discovers that it is not an isolated incident but rather it is a more pervasive HR practice of the company, then TAFEP will watch the company more closely and we will continue to work with them to work through that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Having said that, let me also assure Members that the incidence of discrimination of all forms, based on the cases we see at TAFEP, is still low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The second point about the retirement age, as I had mentioned, the key difference between the retirement age and re-employment age is that retirement age involves same job, same pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Re-employment age is not necessarily the same job, not necessarily the same pay.
